business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Federal-Provincial Jurisdiction: federal common law; Quebec private law governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (civil law tradition); corporate law codified in the Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, and the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, in force 2018)
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, provisionally in force 2017)
Canada-Hong Kong Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2016)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (mandatory declaration of beneficial owners controlling 25% or more); Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, s. 84.2 (register of persons with significant control); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.5 (register of individuals with significant control); Hague Apostille Convention entered into force for Canada on 11 January 2024.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Canadian sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence under FINTRAC guidance; screening records must be retained for a minimum of five years in accordance with PCMLTFA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca for Quebec incorporation; Corporations Canada - www.ic.gc.ca (NUANS name search) for federal CBCA incorporation with registered office in Quebec
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, requires the corporate name to be in French; a name in another language is admissible only if accompanied by a French version in all public documents; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for registration purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name refusal, the applicant may file a new or amended declaration through the REQ portal; within 30 days of receiving the refusal decision, the applicant may demand a review of the decision under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; a further appeal lies to the Administrative Division of the Court of Quebec, and judicial review is available before the Court of Appeal upon leave.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only for the registered office and legal service address, provided a physical street address in Quebec is maintained and no post-office box is used. However, for an ISIC 5210 cross-dock order fulfillment hub, a physical commercial warehouse is mandatory for the actual 3PL operations; no statutory warehousing license is required, but municipal zoning, occupancy and fire safety permits apply.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate - approximately 25% to 40% annual probability of unannounced inspection for an operating warehouse (municipal zoning, fire prevention and CNESST occupational health and safety inspections); below 5% for a purely registered-office address. FINTRAC inspection risk is low because this entity is not a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, principally sections 3-11 concerning constitution and articles, sections 19-20 concerning registered office and records, and applicable provisions governing directors, officers, shares, meetings, and corporate records. A federal alternative is the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a company under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, including the articles and prescribed information submitted through the Registraire des entreprises online incorporation service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Quebec business corporation. Shares may be issued for consideration authorized by the corporation, subject to the articles, directors' approval, and the Business Corporations Act. Quebec does not generally require incorporation capital to be deposited into an escrow account. The corporation should maintain evidence of subscription, payment, and share issuance in its minute book. Banking institutions may impose their own funding and beneficial-owner verification requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscription of the incorporator or subscriber for the number and class of shares specified in the subscription agreement, for the stated consideration, and issue those shares as fully paid upon receipt of consideration. RESOLVED THAT the registered office be established at the Quebec address recorded in the corporate records and filed with the Registraire des entreprises. RESOLVED THAT [Name] be appointed President and [Name] Secretary, each to serve until replacement or resignation. RESOLVED THAT the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute ordinary-course documents, and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select the Quebec or Federal Incorporation Route
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services, or Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre for a federal corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the operating company will be incorporated under Quebec law or federally and registered extra-provincially in Quebec. For a Quebec corporation, confirm the corporate name, Quebec registered office, share structure, director information, and ultimate beneficial ownership information. Conduct a name search and reserve the name if required. A numbered corporation may be used where name clearance is not desired.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names or numbered-company request
Name-search or reservation evidence, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name or use a numbered corporation. If information is incomplete, correct the online application and resubmit before the filing deadline stated by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Submit the Statutory Constitution Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online incorporation portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for constitution of a company, upload or enter the articles and prescribed corporate information, pay the applicable indexed fee, and retain the electronic confirmation. Documents executed outside Quebec should be signed by authorized persons and accompanied by certified translations where required. Notarization is not generally required for the standard Quebec electronic incorporation filing, but signatures and corporate authority should be independently verified.
required_dossiers: Certified translation of non-French or non-English supporting documents, where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the Registrar's online correction or correspondence process. Cure name, address, director, share, or document defects and resubmit the corrected filing. Preserve the query notice and proof of timely response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number and Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate or confirmation of constitution, enterprise number, filed articles, and current enterprise-register extract. Verify the legal name, registered office, directors, business activities, and status. File any required initial declarations or updates within the statutory periods and retain the documents in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Initial declaration or prescribed update, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a correction, amendment, or update to the Registraire des entreprises. If the Registrar refuses a requested correction, use the applicable administrative review or judicial review route after obtaining Quebec counsel advice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Organizational Proceedings and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors and shareholders; corporate records are maintained internally and reflected in the Quebec enterprise register where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or obtain written resolutions. Adopt the registered office, approve the share subscription and consideration, appoint officers, approve banking authorities, adopt signing authorities, establish the fiscal year, approve the minute book, and issue share certificates or electronic ownership records. Record the shareholder register, securities register, director register, and beneficial ownership information.
required_dossiers: Share certificate or electronic issuance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective resolutions by replacement resolutions, ratification, or written consent of the competent corporate body. Reissue inaccurately recorded shares and update the statutory registers without backdating documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Operating Location and Complete Municipal Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality in which the warehouse or cross-dock facility is located; relevant municipal urban-planning, building, occupancy, and fire-prevention departments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning permits warehousing, logistics, loading, vehicle circulation, and storage of the proposed goods. Obtain any certificate of occupancy, renovation or building permit, signage approval, site-plan approval, and municipal business permit required by the municipality. Confirm fire-code requirements before possession or commercial operation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request written reasons for refusal, amend the use, plans, or premises, and seek municipal administrative review or zoning variance where available. Do not occupy or operate contrary to a municipal order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Employer, Workplace, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail, and Canada Border Services Agency where import, export, or bonded-storage activities apply.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain business-number program accounts required for payroll, GST/HST, and Quebec QST. Register with CNESST when the employment facts require coverage. Obtain a Canada Border Services Agency importer-exporter RM account for commercial imports or exports. If storing unreleased imported goods, apply for the appropriate customs sufferance or bonded-warehouse authorization before commencing that activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and enterprise number
Warehouse security, premises, and inventory-control procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected registrations, provide additional identity or premises evidence, and request written reassessment. Do not represent the facility as bonded or customs-authorized until CBSA approval is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single Quebec industrial licensing board regulates ordinary cross-dock or third-party logistics warehousing. The principal authorities are the municipality, the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs, the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail, and the Canada Border Services Agency where customs-controlled storage applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general provincial manufacturing or warehouse operating licence is ordinarily required for standard order-fulfillment and cross-dock operations. Required approvals may include a municipal certificate of occupancy or use, building and fire approvals, and a CBSA customs sufferance or bonded-warehouse authorization if the facility stores goods under customs control.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinary warehouse and cross-dock operations are generally not subject to a full environmental impact assessment. Registration or authorization under the Quebec Environment Quality Act may be required for activities with material environmental effects, including specified wastewater discharges, contaminated-site work, hazardous-material handling, drainage works, fuel installations, or other prescribed activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single warehouse-wide numerical threshold applies. Wastewater must comply with the applicable municipal sewer by-law and Quebec authorization conditions; direct releases to the environment may require authorization under the Environment Quality Act and must not contravene the federal Fisheries Act. VOC and air-emission controls apply where regulated equipment, fuel systems, refrigeration systems, or material-handling processes trigger provincial or federal requirements. Hazardous and residual materials must be segregated, stored, transported, documented, and disposed of through authorized channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, obtain municipal building and occupancy approvals and fire-prevention acceptance, including review of exits, fire alarms, sprinklers, emergency lighting, storage heights, hazardous materials, and fire access. Structural floors, racking, docks, mezzanines, and lifting equipment should be reviewed by qualified professionals and maintained within certified load limits. Workplace compliance requires CNESST occupational-health and safety procedures, training, incident reporting, machine and forklift controls, personal protective equipment, emergency plans, and inspections. Additional approvals may apply to pressure equipment, fuel systems, refrigeration systems, hazardous products, or dangerous-goods transport.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal GST/HST and federal corporate income tax administration (portal: CRA My Business Account / GST/HST NETFILE / Business Registration Online); Revenu Québec – Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec provincial corporate income tax administration (portal: Revenu Québec Cliquez / Trans@ction; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for the enterprise number NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity does not require a Canadian incorporation to obtain a tax id. The foreign supplier that carries on business in Canada or makes taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST. Procedure: (1) file Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or apply online via CRA Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN); add the GST/HST program account (RT-suffix) to the BN. (2) For Quebec Sales Tax, register separately with Revenu Québec using the NEQ assigned at Quebec business registration, or request a QST account (e.g., account number with a 'TQ' identifier) if the person has a Quebec establishment or makes taxable supplies in Quebec above the CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold. (3) Under the July 1, 2021 GST/HST e-commerce framework, a non-resident seller fulfilling Canadian orders through a Canadian cross-dock or fulfillment warehouse is deemed to make supplies in Canada and must register unless the small supplier exception applies; if a distribution platform is used, the platform is the deemed supplier and must register and collect regardless of the seller's revenue. QST rules align with the GST framework via the Quebec Taxation Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a Canadian federal/provincial business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the federal Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act; corporate income is taxed at the entity level and any distribution to shareholders is separately taxed; no flow-through or check-the-box classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections: (1) Excise Tax Act (GST/HST): section 156 election to simplify invoicing between a supplier and a related corporation for direct payment supplies; section 150 election for closely related corporations to elect taxable treatment on intercompany supplies to preserve input tax credits; section 273 election for a member to file GST/HST on behalf of a partnership. (2) Income Tax Act: section 216 election for a non-resident owner of Canadian real property to file a net-basis Part I return rather than Part XIII gross withholding; section 219 branch tax rules for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada; hybrid mismatch limitation under section 18.6 denies deductions for hybrid mismatch arrangements with no opt-out election except as prescribed. (3) Quebec: analogous QST elections under the Quebec Taxation Act for closely related persons and consolidated filing elections. (4) For cross-border e-commerce fulfillment, the corporation may elect simplified accounting methods for associated persons under the GST/HST rules; no election can convert an entity-level taxpayer into a pass-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual federal-provincial value-added tax: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST, Part IX of the Excise Tax Act) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST, administered by Revenu Québec under the Quebec Taxation Act). Quebec is not a participating province for HST, so the combined rate is 5% federal GST plus 9.975% provincial QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 for GST/HST and CAD 30,000 for QST (small supplier threshold) measured by taxable supplies made in Canada in the current calendar quarter or the preceding four calendar quarters (s. 148(1) Excise Tax Act; analogous Quebec rule). A non-resident e-commerce seller using a Canadian warehouse or cross-dock facility is deemed to make supplies in Canada and must register once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded; however, for sales made through a distribution platform, the platform is the deemed supplier and bears the registration and collection obligation regardless of the seller's revenue. Certain non-resident digital-service suppliers may be required to register under the simplified non-resident registration framework, but the small supplier threshold generally applies to goods-fulfillment scenarios.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-approval, digital stamping, or continuous control transaction framework is in force in Canada or Quebec. GST/HST is self-assessed and remitted via CRA Form GST34 (GST/HST Return) through GST/HST NETFILE; QST is self-assessed and remitted to Revenu Québec via its electronic filing channels. Tax invoices must contain prescribed data elements (supplier GST/HST and QST registration numbers, date of supply, description, tax amount or rate). Pan-Canadian e-invoicing based on the PEPPOL standard is voluntary (Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Council initiative) and is being adopted for B2G transactions; Quebec has introduced similar B2G e-invoicing pilots. Non-residents may use a simplified registration process, but all electronic records and source documents must meet CRA and Revenu Québec record-retention requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported by the supplier are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 20 Excise Tax Act when the goods are shipped or delivered to a destination outside Canada by or on behalf of the supplier before use or consumption in Canada. Services supplied to a non-resident are generally zero-rated under section 7, Schedule VI unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada, relates to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or is rendered to an individual present in Canada. Consequently, warehousing, cross-docking, pick-pack, and order-fulfillment services performed on goods physically located in Quebec are taxable at the combined 14.975% rate (GST + QST) even when charged to an overseas e-commerce principal; international freight transportation of goods from Canada to an outside destination is separately zero-rated under section 24 of Schedule VI. To claim zero-rating on the export of goods, the Canadian entity must make a supply that includes the export, retain contemporaneous evidence of export, and ensure the goods are not further manufactured, altered, or used in Canada before export. Input tax credits (ITCs) and Quebec input tax refunds (ITRs) are available on related expenses (inbound logistics, utilities, labour, occupancy) to the extent the expenses support commercial activities, including zero-rated supplies; a net refund arises when ITCs/ITRs exceed output tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration – Canada Border Services Agency B13A/G13 Export Declaration or ACI eManifest export reporting
Commercial Invoice including seller, non-resident buyer, HS classification, value, currency, and Incoterms
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill – through transport document showing the foreign destination and export port of exit
Carrier or freight forwarder proof of export (date of departure, mode of transport, signature, port code)
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign-currency bank receipt or wire transfer confirmation evidencing payment from the non-resident buyer
Cross-dock and warehouse discharge records evidencing physical movement from the Quebec fulfillment facility to the export gateway
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess export zero-rating claims within the normal four-year reassessment period, which is unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, neglect, or wilful default. If the exporter cannot produce the required documents, the zero-rating is reversed, output GST/HST at 5% and QST at 9.975% are reassessed, and arrears interest is charged. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act include: (i) failure to register or file penalties under s. 280 (greater of 5% of the amount owing and $100, plus 1% per month to 12 months); (ii) false statements or omissions under s. 285(1) – 50% of the net tax sought to be evaded (minimum $100); (iii) gross-negligence penalty under s. 285.1 – up to 50% of the understated net tax; (iv) criminal tax evasion under s. 327 – on summary conviction a fine up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months, and on indictment a fine up to $100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Analogous penalties apply under the Quebec Taxation Act through Revenu Québec, including refusal or clawback of input tax refunds (ITRs) and monetary penalties of up to 50% of the tax evaded. Retrospective clawbacks may also disallow input tax credits/refunds on related expenses where the underlying zero-rating is denied, and directors may be liable for unremitted GST/HST and QST under the statutory director-liability provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act, with prudential banking supervision delegated to OSFI and AML/ATF surveillance to FINTRAC; Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration authority because of its free-floating currency regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada grants unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital-account transactions under OECD capital-movement liberalisation norms. Profit remittance, dividends, management fees, and repayment of shareholder loans may flow freely without prior Bank of Canada approval; the only macro-level frictions are Quebec’s source-withholding obligations under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and the arm's-length transfer-pricing requirements for cross-border related-party payments. No bona fide onerous foreign-exchange conversion is imposed on the operational CA_CORP treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio in Canada. CA_CORP may lawfully retain foreign currency receivables offshore or in domestic USD/CAD accounts. Export records remain subject to CBSA import/export reporting, GST/HST zero-rating documentary support, and FINTRAC’s EFT over $10,000 CAD threshold reporting; no exchange-control approval certificate is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintechs such as Airwallex, OFX, and CurrencyCloud are viable only as FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs); they do not hold a Canadian Schedule I banking licence and cannot provide bank-grade escrow protection under CDIC. Legal constraint: core cross-border settlement must ultimately clear through a Canadian bank or a regulated correspondent bank. MSB rails are permissible as an operational efficiency layer for small ACH/Wire disbursements, but prudential capital-admission and controlled FX treasury functions should remain in an OSFI-regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not a blanket FINTRAC mandate; directors may open accounts remotely using certified true corporate records, digital ID attestations, and a board resolution produced under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act. In practice, Quebec-based relationship managers may require a recorded video interview for non-resident beneficial owners, source-of-wealth questioning, and a notarised bank mandate for signatories. The default is a remote-enhanced-due-diligence path with the right to escalate to physical closure at the Chief Compliance Officer's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement between inbound capital and offshore 3PL disbursements without matching inventory or order records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Issued and received commercial invoices, packing lists, order-management system export report, destination-courier tracking data, CBSA customs entry summaries, and quarterly reconciliation statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume Canadian/USD inflows from marketplace settlement accounts with inconsistent beneficial owner names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Marketplace seller agreements, platform payout statements, beneficial-ownership register, CRS/FATCA self-certification, and audited trial balance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-trip funding or third-party disbursement to non-contractual overseas warehouse operators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Warehouse services agreement, per-unit fulfilment tariffs, COGS reconciliation schedule, proof of warehouse possession, watch-list screening results, and a transparent transaction-flow charter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent FX conversion rationale or trades that appear to circumvent standard market-rate execution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authorised FX treasury policy, dealer pre-trade quotations, executed SWIFT confirmations, booking counterparty legal entity details, and monthly mark-to-market valuation report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections flow by SWIFT MT103 from the source bank to a Canadian Schedule I bank account in CAD or USD. No Bank of Canada exchange-control notification is required. The intended purpose code should read 'Contributed capital pursuant to CBCA/QBCA articles; ISIC 5210 overseas warehouse fulfilment; e-commerce 3PL operating entity CA__CA_QC__CA_CORP'. The receiving bank will verify the UETR, source-entity bank credentials, and beneficial-owner ownership chain; funds then clear through Lynx (RTGS) for CAD or the bank's correspondent USD account. Supporting evidence must include the corporate authorising resolution, bank reference letter, and source-of-funds statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: High-value supplier payments use SWIFT MT103 via the operating account with a clear goods-description reference to the underlying overseas warehouse service. Domestic Canadian warehouse rent and payroll use ACSS/EFT and the Real-Time Rail where available. For large capex or inventory-deferred settlements, commercial letters of credit (LCs) are acceptable; for low-value marketplace disbursements, Airwallex API frequency payments and local ACH rails are permissible as supplemental clearing paths. All outbound transactions remain fully traceable because the primary bank statement is the single ledger of record and FATCA/CRS reporting remains aligned to CA_CORP’s tax residency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD and CAD/CNH) with OSFI-regulated counterparties
FX Swaps (overnight/rollover for conversion of export proceeds into CAD)
Cross-Currency Swaps (for USD-denominated shareholder loans or lease obligations)
FX Options and Collars (premium/zero-cost protection on forecast CAD/USD flows)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) solely in pairs where the underlying non-CAD currency is non-convertible onshore, executed through a Canadian bank or FINTRAC-registered MSB; not required for standard CAD/USD trade flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return — Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) Form 22A
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or the date of continuation/amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada; corporation loses legal capacity if struck off; revival fees apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration — Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration with the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fines for legal persons: CAD 500–2,000 for a first offence and CAD 1,000–5,000 for a subsequent offence; persistent failure for three or more years leads to administrative strike-off (radiation).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required if the corporation is a reporting issuer or distributing corporation under Canadian securities laws, or if the shareholders do not unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor. For private CBCA/QBCA corporations, an audit may be dispensed with by unanimous shareholder resolution provided the corporation is not a reporting issuer and the shareholders consent for each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible private corporations; annual financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the chosen framework and be presented to the shareholders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the CBCA, maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC) (holding 25% or more of shares or control), with no annual external UBO filing. Under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the annual updating declaration must confirm and update ultimate beneficial ownership details for individuals holding 25% or more of votes or shares; share transfers occurring during the year are reflected in the next annual updating declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 25,000 for a full statutory audit; USD 2,000 – USD 8,000 for a review engagement if audit exemption applies

stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact registered name as recorded with Corporations Canada / Registraire des entreprises du Québec; use English/French forms.
